title: Effective Context-Sensitive Memory Dependence Prediction
problem: Memory dependence prediction in out-of-order processors suffers from a growing performance gap with ideal predictors (up to 6% for modern architectures). Context-sensitive predictors lack well-adjusted history lengths, causing accuracy loss and high storage requirements.
motivation: Memory dependence prediction is crucial for increasing instruction and memory-level parallelism in high-performance out-of-order processors.
method: PHAST is a memory dependency predictor (a circuit that guesses whether a load instruction will stall waiting for data from an earlier store) that figures out how much instruction history each load needs by finding the most recent store it could depend on. Rather than using a fixed history window for all loads, it customizes this window per-load to reduce storage costs. The team tested it using cycle-accurate simulation (tracking every processor clock cycle) on SPEC CPU 2017 benchmarks, building both a practical 14.5KB version and an unlimited-budget oracle predictor to measure how close the practical design gets to ideal performance.
key_novelty: Each load determines its optimal history window by finding the most recent store it depends on, reducing storage while maintaining accuracy close to an ideal predictor.
contributions: PHAST predictor that dynamically adjusts history length per load for improved accuracy and efficiency
Empirical validation that identifying the youngest conflicting store is sufficient (0.47% gap from ideal with unlimited budget)
Practical 14.5KB implementation achieving only 1.50% gap from ideal performance
62.5%-70% average misprediction reduction and 3.04%-5.05% speedups versus state-of-the-art predictors

metrics.speedup: 5.05% avg vs StoreSets (up to 39.7%), 1.29% avg vs NoSQ (up to 22.0%), 3.04% avg vs MDP-TAGE (up to 38.2%)
metrics.accuracy: 1.50% gap from ideal, 62.5%-70% misprediction reduction on average

primary_theme: context-sensitive memory dependence prediction for out-of-order processors
